Fit a custom tgmrf latent block

Source: R/tgmrf_imh.R
tulpa_tgmrf.Rd

One front door for inference over a user-defined tgmrf() latent block's hyperparameter vector theta. mode selects the inference target and correction:

  • "imh" (default) – Tier-1 pseudo-marginal MCMC against an unbiased importance estimate of p(y | theta), with jointly resampled latent draws.

  • "nuts" – NUTS on the Laplace-approximate theta marginal, followed by PSIS importance correction to the joint posterior. Tier 2: finite weighted approximation. The correction is applied only when its Pareto-k passes the sample-size-dependent reliability threshold.

  • "vi" – Tier-2 structured: a single-path Pathfinder Gaussian fit of the Laplace-approximate theta marginal.

  • "nuts_joint" – Tier-1 exact MCMC sampling the FULL joint (beta, z, theta) against its true density (requires a C++-backend block, see tgmrf_cpp()).

The inference method is an argument, not a parallel verb.

Usage

tulpa_tgmrf(
  y,
  n_trials,
  X,
  block,
  family = "binomial",
  phi = 1,
  re_idx = NULL,
  n_re_groups = 0L,
  sigma_re = 1,
  mode = c("imh", "nuts", "vi", "nuts_joint"),
  control = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

y, n_trials, X

Response, binomial trial counts (or NULL), and the fixed-effect design matrix.

block

A tgmrf() latent block.

family, phi

Observation family and its dispersion.

re_idx, n_re_groups, sigma_re

Optional scalar random-intercept structure.

mode

Inference engine: "imh", "nuts", "vi", or "nuts_joint".

control

A list of numerical / tuning knobs for the chosen mode (e.g. n_iter, warmup, thin, scale for "imh"; epsilon, max_depth, target_accept for the NUTS modes; n_draws, max_lbfgs, lbfgs_tol for "vi"; plus the shared pilot_axis_points, max_iter, tol, n_threads, verbose). An unknown knob for the chosen mode errors rather than being silently ignored.

...

Individual control knobs may also be passed directly by name; they are merged into control (a named argument here wins over the same name inside control).

Value

A tulpa_fit object; $backend and $mode record the engine used. Every mode reports the fixed effects: $draws holds the beta columns first, any retained random effects and latent z, then theta, so coef(), summary() and posterior_sample() read them as on any other fit. "imh" returns the selected IS particle retained by pseudo-marginal MH; "nuts_joint" samples the full joint density. Corrected "nuts" resamples whole joint rows with PSIS weights; $correction_applied, $correction_declined, $pareto_k, $pareto_k_is_ess and $target describe the result. With control$is_correction = FALSE, too few draws, or a k above the gate, NUTS returns its uncorrected Laplace theta chain with Gaussian conditional beta draws, inference_mode = "structured", inference_tier = 2L. Corrected NUTS also remains Tier 2 and carries correction = "psis"; its resampled rows have draws_kind = "iid" and their dependence through the source chain is recorded in $source_index and $source_theta_draws. "vi" returns a Gaussian theta approximation and conditional Gaussian beta draws. $draws_beta, $draws_z (when available) and $draws_theta split the joint rows by block.

The inner IS budget is calibrated at the outer Laplace mode, using repeated independent likelihood estimates. The package setting .TGMRF_IS sets the target log-estimate SD (1.2), initial budget (16), calibration batches (16), ceiling (65536), and t proposal df (7). $is_particles and $log_estimate_sd report the chosen budget and measured SD. Each estimate costs that many exact joint-density evaluations plus one inner mode/precision solve. $inner_solves counts adapter evaluations after the pilot; $is_likelihood_evaluations also includes calibration.

References

Andrieu and Roberts (2009), The pseudo-marginal approach for efficient Monte Carlo computations, Annals of Statistics 37:697-725, doi:10.1214/07-AOS574 . Each MH proposal pays for an unbiased inner estimate and retains that estimate on rejection.

Doucet, Pitt, Deligiannidis and Kohn (2015), Efficient implementation of Markov chain Monte Carlo when using an unbiased likelihood estimator, Biometrika 102:295-313, doi:10.1093/biomet/asu075 . Repeated pilot estimates calibrate the particle budget against log-estimate variability.

Vehtari, Simpson, Gelman, Yao and Gabry (2024), Pareto smoothed importance sampling, JMLR 25(72):1-58, https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v25/19-556.html. NUTS correction pays one IS estimate per retained theta and a tail fit.

Gomez-Rubio and Rue (2018), Markov chain Monte Carlo with the integrated nested Laplace approximation, Statistics and Computing 28:1033-1051, doi:10.1007/s11222-017-9778-y . MCMC with an INLA marginal retains its deterministic approximation error.

Rue, Martino and Chopin (2009), Approximate Bayesian inference for latent Gaussian models by using integrated nested Laplace approximations, JRSS B 71:319-392, doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2008.00700.x . The inner mode and sparse precision solve build the proposal at each theta.

See also

tgmrf() for the block, tgmrf_cpp() for the compiled-block form.

Examples

# \donttest{
# An iid random intercept written as a tgmrf block over 15 groups; the
# inference method is an argument, not a parallel verb. See the
# custom-process article at https://gillescolling.com/tulpa/articles/tgmrf.html.
set.seed(3)
J <- 15L; g <- rep(seq_len(J), each = 6L); n <- length(g); x <- rnorm(n)
y <- rpois(n, exp(0.3 + 0.5 * x + rnorm(J, 0, 0.6)[g]))
blk <- tgmrf(
  Q = function(theta) Matrix::Diagonal(J, exp(-2 * theta[1])),
  prior = function(theta) stats::dnorm(theta[1], 0, 1, log = TRUE),
  init = c(log_sigma = 0), obs_idx = g)
fit <- tulpa_tgmrf(y, rep(1L, n), cbind(1, x), block = blk,
                   family = "poisson", mode = "imh",
                   control = list(n_iter = 300L, warmup = 150L))
mean(exp(fit$draws[, "log_sigma"]))   # posterior mean group SD
# }
